clinical_ontology.claim_boundary: The ontology constrains structured data entry and agent extraction. It does not interpret records, diagnose, or recommend treatment.

general_education.answer_policy: RAG answer with citation; no patient-specific decision.

response_classification.answer_policy: May emit monitor-only pattern signal; abstain if missing response evidence.

response_regression.answer_policy: May emit score only with uncertainty band and claim boundary.

toxicity_classification.answer_policy: May emit toxicity monitoring signal; urgent symptoms route to care team.

genetic_result_organization.answer_policy: Organize fields only; route to genetic counselor/clinician review.

biomarker_explanation.answer_policy: Explain terminology only; no treatment recommendation.

tumor_marker_trend.answer_policy: Context-dependent monitoring only; never diagnose recurrence.

diagnosis_or_prognosis.answer_policy: Blocked. Refer to clinician/emergency services when urgent.

minimum_evidence_standards.claim_boundary: Minimum evidence standards are engineering guardrails that decide when the system may answer, must hedge, or must abstain. They are not clinical practice guidelines.

claim_types.description: General educational explanation without patient-specific decision.
Organizes user-provided data without interpreting it clinically.
Monitor-only signal that requires clinician review and uncertainty language.
Asserts diagnosis, malignancy, metastasis, recurrence, or cancer status.
Gives specific dosage or medication schedule.
Predicts survival, life expectancy, cure chance, or recurrence probability.
Treats VUS or unclear genetic data as a confirmed genetic diagnosis/risk.
Uses tumor marker value alone to claim recurrence/progression.

limitations: Population defaults may differ from the reference ranges printed by a specific laboratory.
Hemoglobin ranges vary by sex, age, pregnancy status, altitude, and clinical context.
Chemotherapy monitoring thresholds can be more conservative than general population reference ranges.
cbc_reference_context_example.claim_boundary: Reference context is for monitoring support only. It is not a diagnosis, treatment recommendation, or replacement for lab-specific and clinician-reviewed ranges.

interaction_rules.message: St. John's wort can affect drug-metabolism pathways and may interact with oncology medicines. Do not start or stop it without oncology-team/pharmacist review.
interaction_rules.clinician_action: Review supplement use against the active medication list.

interaction_rules.message: Grapefruit products can interact with several oral cancer medicines. Ask the oncology team or pharmacist before using them with CDK4/6 inhibitors.
interaction_rules.clinician_action: Check whether the patient is taking a CYP3A-sensitive oral anticancer medicine.

interaction_rules.message: Some supplements may affect bleeding risk or procedures. This system cannot determine safety; review with the care team/pharmacist before use.
interaction_rules.clinician_action: Review bleeding risk, platelet trend, anticoagulants/antiplatelets, and procedure timing.

interaction_rules.message: CBD/cannabis products may interact with medicines or increase sedation/nausea effects. Discuss use with the oncology team/pharmacist first.
interaction_rules.clinician_action: Check product, dose, legality/context, sedating medicines, and oral anticancer medicines.

interaction_rules.message: High-dose antioxidant supplements during chemotherapy or radiation should be reviewed with the oncology team. Do not use them as a replacement for prescribed treatment.
interaction_rules.clinician_action: Clarify supplement dose and timing relative to chemotherapy/radiation.

genetics.boundary_note: Genetic Counseling Readiness organizes information for oncology/genetics review. It does not diagnose inherited risk, interpret variants as medical advice, or recommend treatment changes.
